what_happened: The job "Make steward items above its limit approvable proposals" ended failed. The producer's final report was sent back with two problems. First, one acceptance criterion was unmet or not reported: the rule that anything above the steward's limit is a proposal, whatever kind the model named, had to be stated in a code comment or the design doc, and the steward prompt had to be corrected if it said otherwise. Second, a separate check did not pass or was not reported: cargo fmt --check, cargo clippy and cargo test for the workspace. The event lists no blocker or major findings. Nothing was delivered.
cause: Completion is judged only when the producer's final report is checked against the criteria. Nothing forces the producer to map each criterion to evidence, or to run the workspace checks, before it reports done. A documentation criterion ("state the rule in a comment or doc, fix the prompt if it disagrees") is easy to skip because it has no failing test. The format, lint and test gate is a separate list of checks, and nothing blocks the report until they have run and been recorded. So gaps in either place surface at the end as a failed job, not earlier.
prevention: Add a pre-submission gate in code. The producer cannot send its final report until (1) it has a per-criterion evidence entry for every acceptance criterion (file and line, or test name), and (2) the system itself has run cargo fmt --check, cargo clippy and cargo test and recorded the results. A missing criterion entry or a failing or unrun check sends the job back to the producer immediately, with the specific gap named, before final verification. Give documentation-type criteria a concrete anchor, such as a named test or a grep-able marker, so their absence is detectable.
proposed_request: Add a pre-submission gate to the producer flow. Before a code job's final report is accepted for verification, Athena must (a) require one evidence entry per acceptance criterion, giving a file and line or a test name, and reject the report if any criterion has no entry; and (b) itself run cargo fmt --check, cargo clippy and cargo test for the workspace and record each result, rejecting the report if any check failed or did not run. The rejection must name the missing criterion or failing check and go back to the producer to fix. Then re-run the work of job 20261015-054026-k2ej: state in a code comment or the design doc that anything above the steward's limit is an approvable proposal whatever kind the model named, and correct the steward prompt if it says otherwise. Done when the gate rejects a report with a missing criterion entry and a report with a failing check, the steward rule is documented, and fmt, clippy and test all pass.
